tips.title: Faire des progrès
tips.body: *J'ai **fait des progrès** en maths.* French says *make progress* in the plural — *des progrès*, never *un progrès* here. The opposite is *j'ai des difficultés en …* (I have difficulties in), also plural.

tips.title: Passer, réussir, rater
tips.body: ***Passer** un examen* = to **sit** it. ***Réussir** un examen* = to **pass** it. ***Rater** / **échouer à** un examen* = to fail it. *J'ai passé mon examen* says nothing about the result, and using it to mean *I passed* is the false friend that reverses your sentence.

tips.title: Mieux and meilleur
tips.body: ***Mieux*** is better as an **adverb** — *je travaille **mieux** cette année*. ***Meilleur*** is better as an **adjective** — *j'ai eu de **meilleures** notes*. Verbs take *mieux*, nouns take *meilleur*, and *plus bon* and *plus bien* do not exist.

tips.title: Pour + infinitive as the plan
tips.body: *Pour améliorer mon français, je vais lire en français tous les soirs.* **Pour** + infinitive gives the aim, then the near future gives the action. Two structures, one sentence, and it answers any "how will you improve" question.

tips.title: Le bulletin and its comments
tips.body: A French report — *un bulletin scolaire* — carries a mark out of 20 and a comment: *excellent, très bien, assez bien, passable, insuffisant*, plus *peut mieux faire* (could do better) and *manque de travail* (lack of work). Recognising these is a reading skill worth marks.

why.matters: French marks run from 0 to 20, the report is *le bulletin* with a comment for every subject, and a reading text about a pupil's term will assume you can read both. This topic exists for that, and for three verbs English speakers get wrong: *passer* means to sit an exam, not to pass it, *réussir* is to pass, *rater* is to fail. It also settles *mieux* against *meilleur* and gives the language of improvement, *faire des progrès* and *pour* with an infinitive, which is the shape of any resolution the exam asks for.

examples.title: Quinze sur vingt
examples.body: A French mark is said as a fraction of twenty: *j'ai eu quinze sur vingt en histoire*. The pass is 10, so 15 is comfortable, 12 is fine and 7 is a problem, and the bulletin's comment follows the number: *très bien* from 15, *assez bien* from 12, *passable* at 10, *insuffisant* below. A listening text that says *sept sur vingt* is telling you the pupil is in trouble without using the word.

props.caption: Marks out of twenty, and where the bulletin's comments fall

visual.alt: Three bars to scale: fifteen out of twenty marked très bien, ten out of twenty as the pass, and seven out of twenty marked insuffisant

examples.title: Passer is not pass
examples.body: *J'ai passé mon examen* tells a French reader you sat it, and nothing about the result. To say you passed you need *réussir*: *j'ai réussi mon examen*. To fail is *rater* or *échouer à*. The false friend is so common that examiners read it literally, and a writing answer meant to boast about passing ends up saying nothing. Learn the three as a set with their English, and check *passer* every time you write it.

examples.title: Faire des progrès, and the plan
examples.body: Improvement has a fixed phrase, *faire des progrès*, plural, and a fixed shape for the plan: *pour* with an infinitive for the aim, then the near future for the action. *Pour avoir de meilleures notes, je vais réviser tous les soirs.* *Mieux* goes with a verb, *je travaille mieux*; *meilleur* goes with a noun and agrees, *de meilleures notes*. A resolution built this way has a purpose, a tense and an agreement in one line.

steps.title: Les notes et le bulletin
steps.body:
French marks run **from 0 to 20**, and the report — *le bulletin scolaire* — gives a mark plus a written comment for each subject.

*J'ai eu **quinze sur vingt** en histoire.* The pass is **10 sur 20**, so *douze* is comfortable and *sept* is a problem.

**The comments** on a bulletin: *excellent* (18+), *très bien* (15+), *assez bien* (12+), *passable* (10), *insuffisant* (below 10). Also *peut mieux faire* (could do better), *manque de travail* (lack of work), *élève sérieux* (a serious pupil), *bon trimestre* (a good term).

**The year**: *un trimestre* is a term — there are three. *La rentrée* is the start of the school year, in September.

**Talking about a mark**: *j'ai eu une bonne note en maths* (a good mark), *j'ai eu une mauvaise note*, *ma moyenne est de quatorze* (my average is 14), *j'ai la meilleure note de la classe* (the best mark in the class).

**Progress**: *j'ai fait **des progrès** en français* (I have made progress), *j'ai des **difficultés** en physique*, *je me suis amélioré(e)* (I have improved), *mes notes ont baissé* (have gone down) / *ont augmenté* (have gone up).

steps.title: Les examens
steps.body:
Three verbs are needed here, and English speakers get them wrong constantly.

- ***Passer** un examen* — to **sit** an exam. *J'ai passé trois examens la semaine dernière.*
- ***Réussir** un examen* — to **pass** it. *J'ai réussi mon examen de français !*
- ***Rater** un examen* / ***échouer à** un examen* — to fail it. *J'ai raté le contrôle de maths.*

**The words**: *un examen, un contrôle* (a class test), *une interro* (a short test), *le brevet, le bac, une épreuve* (a paper), *les résultats*.

**Revision**: *réviser* (to revise), *apprendre par cœur* (learn by heart), *faire des fiches* (make revision cards), *relire ses notes* (reread your notes), *s'entraîner* (practise). *J'ai révisé **2 heures** par soir pendant **5 jours*** — 10 hours in all.

**How it went**: *c'était facile / difficile*, *j'étais stressé(e)* (I was stressed), *j'ai manqué de temps* (I ran out of time), *je n'ai pas assez révisé*, *ça s'est bien passé* (it went well).

**Results**: *j'attends mes résultats* (I am waiting for), *j'ai eu de bons résultats*, *je suis déçu(e)* (disappointed), *je suis fier / fière* (proud).

steps.title: Améliorer ses résultats
steps.body:
The second half of the question is always **what you are going to do about it**.

**The aim** — *pour* + infinitive: *pour améliorer mon français, pour avoir de meilleures notes, pour réussir mes examens, pour être moins stressé(e)*.

**The action** — near future: *je vais réviser tous les soirs, je vais faire mes devoirs à l'heure, je vais demander de l'aide au prof* (ask the teacher for help), *je vais participer plus en classe, je vais moins utiliser mon portable*.

**Set phrases with should**: *je devrais travailler plus* (I should work more), *il faudrait que je m'organise*. *Devrais* is a conditional form worth learning whole.

**Comparing**: *mieux* for verbs (*je travaille mieux*), **meilleur** for nouns (*de meilleures notes*, *mon meilleur trimestre*). *Plus bien* and *plus bon* do not exist.

**Help**: *mes parents m'aident*, *je prends des cours particuliers* (private lessons), *je travaille avec un ami*, *le prof m'a donné des conseils* (advice).

**Long term**: *je veux continuer le français au lycée*, *j'espère aller à l'université* (I hope to), *je voudrais devenir ingénieur* (I would like to become — note: no article before a job).

steps.title: Your turn
steps.body:
**Part A.**

1. Write *I got fifteen out of twenty in French*.
2. Write *I made progress* and *I have difficulties*, both in the right plural.
3. Translate: *I sat my exam* and *I passed my exam*.

**Part B.**

4. Compare a mark this term with one last term.
5. Write one sentence with *mieux* and one with *meilleur*.
6. Say how much you revised, with a number.

**Part C.**

7. Write an aim with *pour* + infinitive and an action in the near future.
8. Write what you should do, with *je devrais*.
9. Write six sentences about your progress: a mark, a comparison, a reason, a difficulty, and two things you are going to do.

For question 9, check every *mieux* and *meilleur* against whether it describes a verb or a noun.

visuals.alt: A blank five-row table for the student to write about progress at school

steps.title: Going deeper
steps.body:
**Never write passer to mean pass.** *J'ai réussi mon examen* is the sentence you want. *J'ai passé mon examen* only says you sat it, and examiners read it literally.

**Keep progrès and difficultés plural.** *J'ai fait **des progrès**, j'ai **des difficultés**.*

**Split mieux from meilleur.** *Je travaille **mieux*** (verb) but *j'ai eu de **meilleures** notes* (noun). And *de*, not *des*, before that preceding adjective.

**Quote a number.** *J'ai eu quatorze sur vingt, alors que j'avais onze* — a mark is concrete detail, and *11* to *14* is a rise of 3 points you can state.

**Explain the change.** *J'ai fait des progrès **parce que** j'ai travaillé plus régulièrement.* A mark with no cause is half an answer.

**Aim then action.** *Pour améliorer mon français, je vais lire des articles en français.* *Pour* + infinitive is the purpose structure, and the near future carries the plan.

**Use je devrais and il faudrait que.** *Je devrais m'organiser mieux.* A conditional form used correctly in Year 9 reads as strong control.

**No article before a job.** *Je voudrais devenir ingénieur / prof / médecin* — never *un ingénieur* after *devenir*.

steps.title: Summary
steps.body:
- Marks are **sur 20**; the pass is **10**; the report is *le bulletin scolaire*.
- Comments: *excellent, très bien, assez bien, passable, insuffisant, peut mieux faire, manque de travail*.
- *Un trimestre* = a term; *la rentrée* = the start of the year.
- **Faire des progrès**, **avoir des difficultés** — both plural.
- *Mes notes ont **baissé** / **augmenté**; je me suis amélioré(e).*
- ***Passer*** = sit; ***réussir*** = pass; ***rater / échouer à*** = fail.
- *Un contrôle* = a class test; *une interro* = a short test.
- Revision: *réviser, apprendre par cœur, faire des fiches, relire ses notes*.
- **Mieux** for verbs, **meilleur** for nouns; *de* before a preceding plural adjective.
- **Pour** + infinitive for the aim, near future for the action.
- *Je devrais …*, *il faudrait que je …*
- *Je voudrais devenir ingénieur* — no article before a job.

examTechnique.body:
Give marks as **… sur vingt**, keep **des progrès** and **des difficultés** plural, and never use *passer* to mean pass — that is **réussir**, and failing is **rater**.

Compare with a previous term to show a change, split **mieux** (verbs) from **meilleur** (nouns), and close with **pour** + infinitive plus a near-future plan, or **je devrais** + infinitive.

A mark with no comparison or cause.

examTechnique.grade9Looks: A grade 9 answer quotes a mark out of twenty, sets it against a previous term, and explains the change with a reason in the perfect. It keeps *des progrès* and *des difficultés* plural, uses *réussir* and *rater* correctly, splits *mieux* from *meilleur* with *de* before the preceding adjective, and finishes with *pour* + infinitive and a near-future plan, adding *je devrais* and a long-term aim with no article before the job.
